text:
Gokwe-Kwekwe Bus Crash Death Toll Rises to 10
The death toll from Wednesday morning’s horrific road accident along the Gokwe-Kwekwe Road has risen to 10, police have confirmed.
The fatal collision occurred at around 5AM at the 110-kilometre peg towards Kwekwe when a bus carrying 36 passengers collided with a haulage truck.
Police said eight people initially died at the scene, while two more later succumbed to injuries sustained in the crash.
“Reference is made to the ZRP’s message on X platform regarding a fatal road traffic accident which occurred on 27/05/26 at 0500 hours at the 110 km peg along Gokwe-Kwekwe Road towards Kwekwe. The death toll has risen to 10,” police said in a statement.

Overtaking Attempt Ends in Tragedy
Preliminary investigations indicate that the bus driver allegedly attempted to overtake another vehicle before crashing into the oncoming haulage truck.
The impact left the bus badly damaged, while several injured passengers were ferried to nearby hospitals for treatment.
National police spokesperson Commissioner Paul Nyathi confirmed the accident and said investigations into the circumstances surrounding the collision are still underway.
Another Deadly Week on Zimbabwe’s Roads
The latest tragedy comes as the country continues to record a spike in fatal road accidents.
Just days earlier, eight Roman Catholic congregants died after a Toyota Noah plunged into the Deka River near Hwange.
The accident happened at around 7AM along Deka Road near Deka Bridge when the vehicle, carrying 13 passengers returning from an all-night prayer vigil, reportedly lost control while crossing the bridge.
Police said the vehicle became submerged underwater, resulting in eight deaths, while five survivors were rescued and admitted to Hwange Colliery Hospital for treatment.
Authorities have since arrested the driver of the Toyota Noah in connection with the accident.
Mnangagwa Declares Deka Accident a State of Disaster
President Emmerson Mnangagwa has since declared the Deka Bridge accident a State of Disaster under the Civil Protection Act.
The declaration allows Government to coordinate emergency assistance for bereaved families, facilitate funeral support and provide medical assistance to survivors injured in the crash.
Six More Killed Near Redcliff
Meanwhile, another fatal collision claimed six lives on May 25 along the Harare-Bulawayo Road near the Redcliff turn-off.
Police said a Honda Fit collided with a haulage truck at the 223-kilometre peg at around 5:45PM, killing six people on the spot.
The recent wave of deadly accidents has renewed calls for motorists to exercise caution on the country’s roads, particularly during overtaking and when travelling at night or in the early hours of the morning.
